newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua's Ortega warns of more Peru-style attacks.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua's Ortega warns of more Peru-style attacks.

text.p: Former Sandinista President Daniel Ortega said on Monday the hostage-taking by Marxist rebels in Peru was a wake-up call for Latin America's governments to address the growing gap between rich and poor.

Ortega, who led Nicaragua's 1979-1990 left-wing Sandinista government, called on Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori to heed the demands of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels and warned of more such attacks across the region.
Ortega faced a similar situation as a prisoner 22 years ago.
He was freed in a hostage exchange in 1974 after seven years in jail when Sandinista rebels in Nicaragua took hostages at a Christmas party and successfully negotiated the release of prisoners.

Among the demands of the MRTA rebels, who still hold more than 140 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence, were a restructuring of Peru's economy and the freeing of hundreds of imprisoned fellow rebels.
"The MRTA's proposal ... is indisputably a proposal that should be taken into account by President (Alberto) Fujimori," Ortega told reporters.
Ortega said the growing inequalities and social injustice in Latin America have made the region "fertile ground" for such rebellions.

"I think this situation should be a wake-up call to all of Latin America's governments and economic groups. What is being affirmed here is the need for changes in the political economy and the distribution of the wealth," he said.

Ortega said the Peruvian attack, along with the emergence of guerrilla groups in Mexico and the continued strength of the guerrillas in Colombia, showed that the revolutionary struggle in Latin America is still alive.

Peruvian intelligence services have speculated that some of the MRTA commandos had received training in Nicaragua, a refuge for revolutionaries in the 1980s when the Sandinistas governed with Cuban and Soviet backing.
Ortega said many revolutionaries passed through Nicaragua and some of the MRTA commandos could have done so, but he did not personally remember any of them.
